issues.title: Add public release metadata and clear entry point
issues.summary: The public bundle has no README, LICENSE, CITATION, requirements.txt, or single build/reproduction path.
issues.detail: A reviewer or future session can find the TeX/PDF/data files, but there is no public-facing orientation layer that explains what to build, what is archival, what data is bundled, what dependencies are required, and what claims the package supports.
issues.resolutionApproach: Create a release README with the intended Paper A/Paper B split, exact build command, exact reproduction commands, dependency list, data provenance, checksums, and a public-readiness checklist. Add LICENSE and CITATION files appropriate for a preprint/source bundle.

issues.title: Align the flagship claim with the latest research direction
issues.summary: The manuscript still calls SPARC/galaxy the flagship empirical confrontation, while the latest research says THz residual spectroscopy is the cleanest near-term test.
issues.detail: The newest module stance is formal SK spectral measure -> neutrino assignment gate -> THz residual template -> gauge-safe spectroscopy bound, with galaxy quarantined until an IR scale bridge is derived. Public text that foregrounds SPARC as the flagship sends the wrong credibility signal.
issues.resolutionApproach: Revise abstract, reader map, principal results, scope table, and SPARC section headings so Paper A foregrounds the formal core and THz residual-template search. Move SPARC to a quarantined Paper B lane or label it as diagnostics only.

issues.title: Replace branched-cover generation claim with magnetized-torus index route
issues.summary: The manuscript still foregrounds branched-cover generation counting, but the research gate says generations need index/projection/anomaly machinery.
issues.detail: Branched covers can remain as geometry or projection language only if they act on the zero-mode Hilbert space. They should not independently multiply generation count alongside flux degeneracy.
issues.resolutionApproach: Rewrite title/abstract/appendix references to make magnetized compactification the first toy matter route. Add a compact table: flux integers, projected zero-mode dimension, Yukawa-rank check, charge conservation, anomaly condition, and current status.

issues.title: Fix neutrino benchmark/window inconsistency
issues.summary: The manuscript benchmark uses nu3 = 0.30, while nearby text claims the restricted window is nu2,nu3 in [0.05,0.2].
issues.detail: This is a simple but high-risk consistency bug. A critical reader can catch it immediately, and it affects the credibility of the assignment catalog and any locked alpha statement.
issues.resolutionApproach: Replace the benchmark with a point inside the declared window, or change the declared window and rerun the assignment table. Then propagate alpha, mu_eff, mass sum, THz lines, and skipped-mode statements from one live catalog.

issues.title: Unify A1/A4/A7/A8 assignment catalog across manuscript sections
issues.summary: The paper needs one source of truth for assignments, alpha, mu_eff, skipped modes, and THz template lines.
issues.detail: Earlier segmentation identified a neutrino/THz assignment mismatch. Cycle 012 generated a better assignment gate, but the manuscript has not yet been reconciled section-by-section.
issues.resolutionApproach: Generate a manuscript-ready assignment appendix from the CSV, then replace all local numeric claims with references to the live table. Include branch status and which skipped modes are forbidden, heavy, or weakly coupled.

issues.title: Remove any direct standard LED photon-line framing
issues.summary: Literal THz compact radii fail the standard minimal LED scale gate.
issues.detail: Cycle 012 found that the roughly 12.1 THz anchor is tied to the atmospheric splitting, but literal micron-scale radii conflict with minimal neutrino LED constraints.
issues.resolutionApproach: State consistently that THz lines are induced compact-sector spectroscopy templates, not direct photon emission from a minimal neutrino KK radius. Add a short scale-gate paragraph near the first THz claim.

issues.title: Add selection rules or suppression ceilings for skipped low modes
issues.summary: A7 and A8 skip low modes; without rules or bounds, those modes become sterile/light-state falsifiers.
issues.detail: The latest assignment gate highlights A7 as especially risky because the skipped (1,0) mode sits close to the solar state.
issues.resolutionApproach: For every skipped low-winding mode, mark it as forbidden, heavy, or weakly coupled. Add numerical coupling ceilings where weakly coupled. Reject branches that cannot meet sterile and cosmology constraints.

issues.title: Execute the molecular/instrumental residual search
issues.summary: The THz pipeline is well framed, but no HITRAN/HITEMP/ExoMol/CDMS/JPL overlap and residual test has been run.
issues.detail: The paper can credibly propose a search, but it should not imply validation until catalog masks, nuisance covariance, injection recovery, and false-alarm tests exist.
issues.resolutionApproach: Start with catalog overlap in 66.7-433.7 cm^-1 and 2,000,000-13,000,000 MHz. Produce a table of masked/unmasked candidate teeth and a first null-bound plan.

issues.title: Benchmark EM/time-varying-media claims against accelerating-wave baseline
issues.summary: The Optica accelerating-wave paper gives a standard-physics account of proper-time-like wave behavior, forward-time solutions, interface continuity, and apparent curved-spacetime effects in time-varying media.
issues.detail: This strengthens the UFT optical/perception and THz lanes by giving them a sharper baseline, but it also creates a weakness: UFT cannot treat time asymmetry, wave slowing, local energy changes, or effective curved-spacetime language as distinctive unless those effects survive the standard accelerating-wave/time-varying-media model.
issues.resolutionApproach: Add a subsection or appendix that models ordinary accelerating-wave/time-varying-media optics first, including pump/material energy accounting, loss, dispersion, interface acceleration, and detector nuisance terms. Only then introduce a compact-phase projector P_EM_timevary(Omega; n(t), pump, loss, detector) and define residual observables or null bounds beyond that baseline.

issues.resolutionApproach: Either implement the documented CLI or rewrite the appendix to call the actual scripts: sparc_reproduce.py for profile extraction, sparc_fit_competitors.py for v103, and sparc_fit_2band.py for v104. Add smoke-test commands.

issues.title: Tighten formal-core theorem language
issues.summary: The formal result is strong inside an admissible class, but should not read like a fully derived UFT theorem.
issues.detail: The latest research says do not write that compact phases prove no-signaling unless microscopic structure is explicit. Positive noise permits correlations; retarded response controls signaling.
issues.resolutionApproach: Add a scope box before formal theorems: assumptions, what is proven, what is selected by admissibility, and what remains conjectural. Insert the SK toy model as the cited worked example.

issues.title: Add optical/perception measurement channel with standard-QM baseline
issues.summary: Tom's observation about photons reflecting from objects and entering human vision is valuable, but the manuscript must distinguish ordinary scattering/decoherence/classical information from compact-phase claims.
issues.detail: A photon that reaches the eye is correlated with the object it scattered from, and the object's absorption/reflection spectrum shapes the information available to perception. In standard quantum theory this is not usually a persistent useful object-human entanglement; environmental decoherence turns the interaction record into robust classical information. The compact-phase theory can use this as a measurement-channel example only if it predicts something beyond ordinary QED material response and detector processing.
issues.resolutionApproach: Add a short subsection or appendix called Optical perception as a measurement channel. Start with the baseline chain object/material states -> scattering/absorption -> photon state -> retinal molecules -> neural classical record. Then define the compact-phase extension as an optional projector P_visual or P_EM-scatter acting on dmu(Omega), with proposed falsifiers: no residual phase-memory correlations after ordinary optical/material/detector nuisance models, wrong spectral structure, or any claim implying controllable signaling.

overviewArticle.title: A Plain-Language Overview Of The Compact-Phase UFT Paper
overviewArticle.lede: This paper asks whether some of the patterns we see in physics could come from a hidden internal phase structure attached to ordinary spacetime. The most mature version is not a final theory of everything; it is a disciplined effective-field-theory program with a shared spectral object, explicit projections into observable channels, and tests that can fail.

sections.heading: The core idea
sections.body: The theory keeps ordinary spacetime and ordinary causal time. It adds two compact internal phase directions, best thought of as hidden resonator coordinates rather than places or extra operational times. When those compact degrees of freedom are traced out, visible physics can inherit memory kernels, noise correlations, and discrete frequency fingerprints.

sections.heading: The organizing insight
sections.body: The strongest insight is that every domain should draw from the same source object: a nonnegative spectral measure dmu(Omega). Neutrinos, spectroscopy, matter structure, gauge tests, and possible gravity response should not each get private spectra. Each domain must declare a projector P_X(Omega), an observable, and a falsifier.

sections.heading: What makes it different
sections.body: Many speculative theories try to explain several anomalies by adding separate mechanisms. This framework is different because it forces cross-domain bookkeeping. The same hidden spectrum may be seen differently by different experiments, but incompatible spectra or unexplained private scales count against the theory rather than being patched in.

sections.heading: What the theory may explain
sections.body: In its best current form, the theory suggests that rest-mass scales and some spectral features could arise from compact-phase standing patterns. It also gives a way to talk about hidden memory and correlations without faster-than-light signaling: correlations live in the noise/correlation kernel, while controllable response must remain retarded.

sections.heading: The cleanest test
sections.body: The cleanest near-term path is THz/far-IR residual spectroscopy. The paper should not claim that one molecular-looking line proves anything. The better claim is a rigid residual template: after known molecular and instrumental structure is modeled and projected out, does a correlated compact-phase frequency pattern survive?

sections.heading: What has already been analyzed
sections.body: The work has already gone through a segmentation audit, a 10k-plus external theory-corpus pass, a formal SK toy-kernel checkpoint, a neutrino/THz assignment gate, a THz residual-search design, a magnetized-torus matter-sector gate, a projector ledger, and a public-readiness package audit. The SPARC galaxy module also has executed four-galaxy diagnostic fits, including a falsified single-band closure and a partially viable two-band closure.

sections.heading: Main strengths
sections.body: The strongest parts are the explicit claim discipline, the shared spectral-measure grammar, the willingness to quarantine weaker modules, the move from line spotting to matched-filter residual statistics, and the recognition that matter generations need real index/projection/anomaly machinery.

sections.heading: Main weaknesses
sections.body: The paper is still too broad as a public first release. The galaxy bridge is not derived, the matter sector needs a clean zero-mode toy model, the neutrino assignment needs a live global scan, spectroscopy needs catalog/residual execution, and the release bundle needs basic public-package hygiene.

sections.heading: Best publication direction
sections.body: The strongest path is to split the project. Paper A should be the formal compact-phase influence-kernel EFT plus THz residual-template falsification and the minimal neutrino assignment gate. Paper B should hold galaxy phenomenology until the IR bridge, full SPARC sample, RAR/lensing tests, and local-gravity closure are ready.

insights.title: Optical perception as a compact-phase channel test
insights.summary: Reflected photons carry object information into detectors and eyes through ordinary scattering, absorption, and decoherence. The theory can use this as a strong explanatory bridge only if compact phase predicts residual spectral, temporal, or correlation structure beyond standard QED material response.
supportingSignals: Human observation validates the broader idea that we infer reality through channel-filtered records, not direct access to objects.
The paper already uses projector language that can model object -> photon -> detector chains.
The photon/eye observation helps explain why compact-phase claims must be operational and falsifiable.
nextInvestigations: Write a baseline measurement-chain subsection for object, scattered photon, retina/detector, and classical record.
Define P_visual or P_EM-scatter as an optional compact-phase projector acting on dmu(Omega).
Reject any claim that implies controllable signaling or persistent useful human-object entanglement without a measurable residual.

insights.title: THz residual templates remain the best near-term public test
insights.summary: The induced THz/far-IR template lane is currently the cleanest way to let the paper make a strong empirical claim while staying honest about amplitude and nuisance models.
supportingSignals: A stable roughly 12.1 THz anchor appears in the A1/A4/A7/A8 assignment gate.
The residual-search pipeline already defines nuisance projection and matched-filter logic.
A null result still improves the paper because it becomes a bound on compact-channel coupling.
nextInvestigations: Run molecular catalog overlap against HITRAN/HITEMP/ExoMol/CDMS/JPL windows.
Add injection-recovery and phase-scrambled false-alarm tests.
Keep line strength as a bound parameter until a measured residual survives catalog and instrument projection.

insights.title: The shared spectral measure is the theory's strongest differentiator
insights.summary: The theory is most credible when all domains draw from the same nonnegative dmu(Omega) and declare their projector, observable, nuisance model, and falsifier.
supportingSignals: This discipline separates the paper from theories that add independent explanations for unrelated anomalies.
The 10k corpus synthesis repeatedly pointed to projector, selection-rule, and constraint-closure patterns.
The SK toy-kernel lane can make the formal claim conditional and referee-readable.
nextInvestigations: Convert the projector ledger into a manuscript table.
For every claimed channel, list observable_X, P_X(Omega), nuisance model, and falsifier.
Mark private spectra or unexplained scales as theory debt rather than tolerated patches.

insights.title: Skipped compact modes are a decisive theory gate
insights.summary: A7/A8 assignment branches can remain interesting only if skipped low modes are forbidden, lifted, or weakly coupled below sterile and cosmology bounds.
supportingSignals: The assignment gate gives a useful catalog of branch risks instead of hiding them.
The neutrino mass-splitting anchor creates a compact-frequency scale that can feed spectroscopy.
The theory becomes stronger if it can explain why visible modes are selected rather than simply chosen.
nextInvestigations: Run one live NuFIT/sterile/cosmology scan from the assignment CSV.
Add branch-by-branch skipped-mode status and coupling ceilings.
Reject branches that cannot satisfy sterile, cosmology, and mass-sum constraints.

insights.title: Generation structure should be rebuilt through zero-mode index checks

supportingSignals: The matter-sector gate already identified flux-index machinery as the cleaner route.
The paper's current caveats about anomaly cancellation can become a strength if formalized.
A single toy model would do more for credibility than broad generation-count speculation.
nextInvestigations: Compute one toy zero-mode spectrum, chirality count, and Yukawa rank.

Use branched covers only as optional projection/geometric language unless they are mathematically tied to the zero-mode Hilbert space.

insights.title: Galaxy response is valuable only after the IR bridge is real

A derived collective or environmental IR mechanism would be a major differentiator if it works.

insights.title: Any electromagnetic compact-channel claim must pass Ward and precision bounds
insights.summary: The photon/perception and THz lanes both touch electromagnetic observables, so the paper should make gauge safety a first-class constraint rather than an afterthought.
supportingSignals: The 10k corpus repeatedly identified gauge/Lorentz safety and precision bounds as common failure modes.
A transverse conserved projector lets the theory discuss EM leakage without immediately breaking known constraints.
Precision null tests can turn speculative channel coupling into bounded parameters.
nextInvestigations: Add Ward identity and transverse-projector rows to the channel ledger.

insights.title: The 11,835-source SQL corpus should drive targeted deep reads
insights.summary: The database is best used as an investigation map: search by theory concept, identify representative sources, then deep-read and cite only the papers that actually support or challenge a claim.
supportingSignals: The corpus stores lane, factor tags, solution tags, abstracts, and similarity edges.
The new SQL Data tab makes the corpus recoverable and searchable inside the dashboard process.
Corpus metrics and reading panes help a future session resume without re-discovering source paths.
nextInvestigations: Search for retarded kernels, open systems, compactification, THz spectroscopy, gauge constraints, and index theorems.
Promote only deep-read papers into manuscript citations.
Use negative examples from the corpus to sharpen falsifiers and avoid overclaiming.

insights.title: Accelerating-wave optics is now a required UFT baseline
insights.summary: Koivurova, Robson, and Ornigotti show that time-varying wave speed can produce proper-time-like behavior, forward-time solutions, conserved wave-frame momentum, and effective curved-spacetime descriptions inside ordinary wave mechanics. UFT can use this as a powerful bridge, but only as a baseline that compact-phase residuals must exceed.
supportingSignals: The paper validates that optical media can naturally generate observer-frame/time-frame distinctions without invoking compact dimensions.
Its forward-time-only accelerating-wave solutions resonate with UFT retarded-response discipline and no advanced controllable signaling.
Its pumped-medium energy accounting supports the UFT rule that local apparent energy changes require a global environment or compact-sector budget.
Photonic time crystals and epsilon-near-zero media provide plausible laboratory platforms for comparing standard predictions to compact-phase residuals.
nextInvestigations: Derive an optical/time-varying-media limit of UFT and show it reduces to the accelerating-wave equation when compact coupling is zero.
Define P_EM_timevary(Omega; n(t), pump, loss, detector) and residual observables after standard medium response is modeled.
Use null tests in pumped photonic media to bound compact-channel coupling rather than claiming broad arrow-of-time evidence.
Keep this as support for channel/projector discipline, not evidence that two compact internal phase directions exist.

recheckCycle.title: UFT paper recheck cycle
recheckCycle.summary: A refined cycle for continuing the paper without losing state: recover the dashboard and source context, take in new observations or papers, rank issues, work only the selected queue unless Tom expands it, verify the manuscript and evidence, update history/score/issues, then hand the next review queue back to Tom.
recheckCycle.refinedFrom: Combined from RECOVERY.md, Tom's repeated review/select/submit-next-round instructions, the standing dashboard workflow in memory, and the current issue-submission process.

steps.name: Recover state
steps.summary: Start by reading dashboard-state.json, MEMORY/daily notes, RECOVERY.md, selectedIssueIds, lastFixSubmission, scoreHistory, history, sources, and active SQL/research paths.

steps.name: Intake new evidence
steps.summary: Add new papers, observations, or session findings to SQL, notes, Insights, supporting data, and history before drawing conclusions.

steps.name: Rank and scope
steps.summary: Review all open issues by rank and severity, preserve Tom's persisted issue filters, and treat selectedIssueIds as the approved next-round work queue.

steps.name: Resolve selected work
steps.summary: Apply fixes to the manuscript, research artifacts, SQL data, notes, or dashboard only for selected or newly necessary issues, keeping claim posture conservative.

steps.name: Verify and re-score
steps.summary: Run available builds, JSON/SQL checks, source probes, citation/package checks, and theory consistency checks; update publish score only when readiness materially changes.

steps.name: Log and hand off
steps.summary: Append history, maintain recovery paths, keep issueViewPreferences and selectedIssueIds durable, and leave Tom a clear list of what changed and what to review next.

recheckCycle.completionRule: A recheck cycle is complete only after selected work is resolved or explicitly deferred, verification has run where available, dashboard history/supporting data/issues/score are updated, and Tom has a recoverable next-round review state.
